item.title: Sure, Turkmen Can Get Visas to Visit the US Again. It May Cost $15,000.
item.description: The visa bond pilot program mandates that otherwise eligible applicants for business or tourism visas from select countries, now including Turkmenistan, will have to post a bond of up to $15,000 in order to enter the United States.

item.title: The Taliban’s ‘Successful’ 2025 Was Anything But
item.description: Last year was actually one of increased isolation, regional tensions, and strategic failure.

item.title: How China and the US Can Make AI Safer for Everyone
item.description: Trump and Xi have agreed in principle to AI talks. A “smart” security agenda would cut shared risk, not U.S. leverage.

item.title: China Backs Pakistan’s Regional Ambitions as ‘All-Weather’ Ties Deepen
item.description: Beijing does not seem worried about Islamabad’s warming ties with the US at this stage.

item.title: Eyeing Local Elections, PPP Leader Makes Half-hearted Apology Over Martial Law
item.description: The leader of the People Power Party, who repeatedly defended Yoon Suk-yeol, delivered his apologies to the public. However, he did not admit the illegitimacy of martial law.

item.title: The US Raid on Venezuela: The View From Beijing
item.description: The U.S. capture of Maduro is likely to bolster, rather than undermine, deterrence across the Taiwan Strait.

item.title: US Expands Visa Bond List to Include Bangladesh, Tonga, and Kyrgyzstan, Among Other Asian Countries
item.description: While the pilot program largely targets countries in Africa, the latest expansion includes countries in Central Asia, South Asia, and the Pacific.

item.title: Building Mongolia’s New, Old Capital at Kharkhorum
item.description: Mongolia wants to resurrect the ancient capital of the Mongol Empire as a modern-day urban hub.

item.title: Why China’s Exploitative Labor System Gives It a Strategic Edge
item.description: China’s decisive source of global competitive advantage lies in its weak labor protections. And it’s driving a race to the bottom for labor rights.

item.title: Violence in Northern Afghanistan Pits Locals Against Gold Mining Operators and the Taliban
item.description: At least four were killed in a recent outbreak of violence between locals and a gold mining company allegedly backed by the Taliban.
